story: A great spiritual leader and prophet came to a confederation of peoples, and one of the first he met was a wild man who was a cannibal, known as "the man who eats humans." The prophet climbed onto the roof of the man's cabin and looked down through the smoke hole, where a large kettle of water sat for cooking human flesh. When the wild man came home, he looked into the water and saw the prophet's face reflected back, mistaking it for his own. In that face he saw beauty, wisdom, and strength, and felt shame for his cannibalism. The prophet came down, sat with him, and taught him the Great Law of Peace. The man accepted the message and agreed to help spread it among his own people, while the prophet, who suffered a speech impediment, went to convert other nations. The chief of one nation was a cruel tyrant, twisted in body and mind, with living snakes in his hair. The prophet charged the reformed man with converting this tyrant, giving him a new name meaning "he who combs." The tyrant, through magic, caused the deaths of the man's three daughters and his wife. Grief-stricken, he wandered stringing wampum, seeking someone to perform a ceremony of condolence. He found the prophet among another people, who comforted him with words of healing, gifted him whelk shells as symbols of purity, and had him place them on his eyes, ears, and throat. Together they composed laws and a peace hymn, then traveled to unite five nations. A solar eclipse helped convince one reluctant nation, and the tyrant was persuaded to join by being offered the position of principal chief; his mind was made straight and the snakes combed from his hair.
